symptom: Suspected, not reproduced: Agent Editor 2.7 stores an agent's test sets as a top-level `testSets` array in its Contents JSON, which mxcli does not model, so re-running `create or modify agent`, `create or replace agent` or `alter agent` might delete them.
file: mdl/backend/modelsdk/agenteditor_carry.go (carryStoredContents, unchanged) via agenteditor_write.go writeCustomBlob; test mdl/executor/issue2266_agent_testsets_test.go
cause: No defect: every agent rewrite reaches UpdateAgentEditorAgent -> writeCustomBlob(update=true), which merges the rebuilt Contents onto the stored one, and a key absent from agentContentsSpec.modelled passes through as stored bytes. `create or replace agent` is the same handler as `create or modify` (the visitor sets CreateOrModify for both); no rename or move sweep rewrites agent Contents.
insight: **A new key Agent Editor adds is already safe when it is top-level and unmodelled** — the #2021 carry is a whitelist of what the encoder writes, not of what it keeps, so the question for each Agent Editor release is only whether a new key lands *inside* a modelled list entry (tools/knowledgebaseTools, paired by id) or a modelled object, which also pass through. Answer such a question by asking the write path, not by reading it: seed the stored unit with the key via GetRawUnitBytes/UpdateRawUnit and run the real statement against a real project. The fixture project is 11.6, under the 11.9 gate every agent statement checks, so wrap the modelsdk backend in a struct that overrides only ProjectVersion. Control: discarding carryStoredContents' result in writeCustomBlob fails all three rewrites (create or modify, create or replace, alter) with testSets and futureKey deleted; a fresh `create agent` writes no testSets.
